scenario.name: SpecterOps, Mandiant & Microsoft — Entra Connect (Azure AD Connect) MSOL_ DKM Decryption & Seamless SSO Silver Ticket
scenario.shortSubtitle: SpecterOps · Dirk-jan Mollema · Mandiant · LocalDB mms_management_agent · DPAPI cryptKeySet & AZUREADSSOACC$
scenario.overview: Imagine a courier bridge building connecting an on-premises castle registry to a rooftop cloud headquarters. Inside the bridge cellar sits a locked database holding the courier master password that syncs every castle citizen into the cloud; an intruder breaks into the bridge building, uses the bridge own built-in unscrambling lens to read that courier password aloud, empties the castle ledger, and stamps forged seamless-entry passes straight into the cloud tower. In this scenario (T1556.007, SpecterOps, Mandiant & Microsoft, Entra Connect (Azure AD Connect) MSOL_ DKM Decryption & Seamless SSO Silver Ticket), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: querying the ADSync SQL LocalDB as NT, then loading mcrypt.dll in PowerShell, then executing MSOL_ DCSync. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Querying the ADSync SQL LocalDB as NT, then Loading mcrypt.dll in PowerShell, then Executing MSOL_ DCSync, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: QUERYING ADSYNC LOCALDB (MMS_MANAGEMENT_AGENT) BLOBS
stages.subtitle: Connecting to SQL LocalDB pipe as NT SERVICE\ADSync to read encrypted connector XML
stages.description: After gaining administrator keys on the directory-sync bridge server, the intruder impersonates the local sync clerk to open the cellar database drawer holding the encrypted courier secret and its locked key wrapper. After obtaining local administrator access on the Entra Connect server (CORP-AADC01), the attacker elevates to NT SERVICE\ADSync (the service account that owns the local SQL Server Express LocalDB instance and the Windows DPAPI user keyset), connects to the named pipe np:\\.\pipe\LOCALDB#...\tsql\query, and queries SELECT private_configuration_xml, encrypted_configuration FROM mms_management_agent alongside keyset_id, instance_id, and entropy from mms_server_configuration. Many organizations mistakenly place their Entra Connect server in a standard Tier-1 server OU managed by general server administrators, unaware that local admin on Entra Connect equates to Domain Admin + Cloud Global Admin. In the documented Sysmon EID 1 exchange from On-Prem Foothold Operator to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with ACK PID 5812 (confirming that the SQLLOCALDB_PIPE_ENUM request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 DPAPI & MCRYPT.DLL DECRYPTION OF MSOL_ CONNECTOR PASSWORD). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ SQLLOCALDB_PIPE_ENUM / ⇠#1 ACK PID 5812) from Node ① (#1 On-Prem Foothold Operator) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Defender for Identity & Sentinel SIEM).

stages.title: DPAPI & MCRYPT.DLL DECRYPTION OF MSOL_ CONNECTOR PASSWORD
stages.subtitle: Reflecting KeyManager in mcrypt.dll to decrypt the on-prem MSOL_9a8b7c6d5e4f password
stages.description: Rather than breaking the encryption mathematically, the intruder loads the bridge server own official decryption library directly into a script, letting the bridge politely unwrap and hand over the plaintext MSOL master courier password. Running as NT SERVICE\ADSync, the attacker uses PowerShell reflection (or AADInternals / adconnectdump) to load C:\Program Files\Microsoft Azure AD Sync\Bin\mcrypt.dll, calls KeyManager.LoadKeySet() (which reads the DPAPI-protected AES key from HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Ad Sync\Shared and unprotects it via CryptUnprotectData), and invokes DecryptBase64ToString() on encrypted_configuration to reveal the plaintext password of the on-premises connector account CORP\MSOL_9a8b7c6d5e4f. Because miiserver.exe must decrypt the MSOL_ password unattended whenever the service restarts, the entire decryption chain resides locally on the Entra Connect host. In the documented Sysmon EID 7 (ImageLoad) exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to Entra Connect Server (ADSYNC), Entra Connect Server (ADSYNC) responds with ACK Signed: Microsoft (confirming that the MCRYPT_DLL_LOADED_BY_PS request succeeded on Entra Connect Server (ADSYNC) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 MSOL_ DCSYNC & AZUREADSSOACC$ SEAMLESS SSO CLOUD PIVOT). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ MCRYPT_DLL_LOADED_BY_PS / ⇠#2 ACK Signed: Microsoft) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Entra Connect Server (ADSYNC)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Defender for Identity & Sentinel SIEM).
stages.mitreTechniqueName: Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files / Registry

stages.title: MSOL_ DCSYNC & AZUREADSSOACC$ SEAMLESS SSO CLOUD PIVOT
stages.subtitle: Using MSOL_ to DCSync AZUREADSSOACC$ and forge Kerberos Silver Tickets into Entra ID
stages.description: Armed with the courier password, the intruder synchronizes every single password hash out of the on-premises castle vault, lifts the cloud seamless-login stamp, and mints forged cloud passes that walk straight into corporate cloud mailboxes without typing a password. Because Password Hash Synchronization (PHS) requires the CORP\MSOL_9a8b7c6d5e4f account to hold Replicating Directory Changes and Replicating Directory Changes All on the domain root, the attacker uses the decrypted MSOL_ credentials to perform a DCSync attack (MS-DRSR DRSGetNCChanges) against CORP-DC01, dumping the NTLM/AES256 hash of the AZUREADSSOACC$ computer account (the shared Kerberos trust bridge created when Entra Seamless Single Sign-On is enabled, allowing the attacker to forge Kerberos Silver Tickets holding any synchronized user’s immutableId and sid to log directly into Entra ID without knowing their password). Microsoft recommends treating Entra Connect as a Tier-0 asset, disabling Seamless SSO in favor of Primary Refresh Tokens (PRT), and rotating the AZUREADSSOACC$ Kerberos decryption key every 30 days. In the documented WinSec EID 4662 (DCSync) exchange from Entra Connect Server (ADSYNC) to DPAPI & mcrypt.dll Keyset Engine, DPAPI & mcrypt.dll Keyset Engine responds with ACK AccessMask 0x100 (confirming that the MSOL_DCSYNC_AZUREADSSOACC request succeeded on DPAPI & mcrypt.dll Keyset Engine and completing the final execution objective of SpecterOps, Mandiant & Microsoft, Entra Connect (Azure AD Connect) MSOL_ DKM Decryption & Seamless SSO Silver Ticket). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ MSOL_DCSYNC_AZUREADSSOACC / ⇠#3 ACK AccessMask 0x100) from Node ③ (#3 Entra Connect Server (ADSYNC)) to Node ④ (#4 DPAPI & mcrypt.dll Keyset Engine), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Defender for Identity & Sentinel SIEM).
stages.mitreTechniqueName: Modify Authentication Process: Hybrid Identity (Seamless SSO)

detectionRule.title: Suspicious Access to Azure AD Connect LocalDB Instance
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Azure AD Connect ADSync LocalDB Enumeration
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\SqlLocalDB.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'ADSync'
  condition: selection
detectionRule.mitigation: Isolate Entra Connect servers as Tier-0 assets with zero non-Tier-0 local administrators.

detectionRule.title: Entra Connect mcrypt.dll Loaded by Non-Sync Process (ADConnectDump / AADInternals)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Azure AD Connect Cryptography DLL Loaded by Uncommon Process
logsource:
  category: image_load
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ImageLoaded|endswith: '\Microsoft Azure AD Sync\Bin\mcrypt.dll'
  filter:
    Image|endswith: '\miiserver.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter
detectionRule.mitigation: Alert immediately if any process other than miiserver.exe loads mcrypt.dll or reads HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Ad Sync\Shared.
